note: Every statement below was read on the linked official source during this session, except where the verification label says otherwise. Quotations are verbatim.

facts.statement: For any permit application filed on or after 1 January 2026 the 2025 California Codes and the 2025 San Francisco Code Amendments apply, with no grace period.
facts.verbatim_quote: If you file on or after January 1, 2026, you must use the 2025 California Codes and the 2025 San Francisco Code Amendments. There is no grace period.

facts.statement: The 2025 Triennial Edition of Title 24 was published on 1 July 2025 and took effect on 1 January 2026; the 2022 edition is now superseded.
facts.verbatim_quote: The 2025 California Building Standards Code (Cal. Code Regs., Title 24) will be published July 1, 2025, with an effective date of January 1, 2026.

facts.topic: Plumbing code sections that govern this work
facts.statement: In the 2025 California Plumbing Code, Chapter 4 (Plumbing Fixtures and Fixture Fittings) contains 404.0 Waste Fittings and Overflows (404.2 Overflows; 404.2.1 Sinks, Lavatories, and Bathtubs) and 409.0 Bathtubs and Whirlpool Bathtubs (409.2 Waste Outlet; 409.3 Overflow; 409.6 Installation and Access).
facts.verbatim_quote: 409.0 Bathtubs and Whirlpool Bathtubs. — 409.2 Waste Outlet. — 409.3 Overflow. — 409.6 Installation and Access. / 404.0 Waste Fittings and Overflows. — 404.2 Overflows. — 404.2.1 Sinks, Lavatories, and Bathtubs.
facts.verification: OFFICIAL-VERIFIED (section titles read from the official table of contents; the full section text was not rendered in this session — see FL-04)

facts.statement: The 2025 San Francisco Plumbing Code is the locally amended plumbing code that applies in San Francisco; it sits alongside the 2025 California Plumbing Code.
facts.verification: OFFICIAL-VERIFIED as the applicable code (link published by the City at sf.gov); section text NOT retrieved — see FL-04

facts.topic: When a plumbing permit is not required (DBI)
facts.statement: DBI's published position is that a permit is not required for minor plumbing work that does not require cutting into or removal of piping; the Plumbing Inspection Division decides the requirement for a specific scope.
facts.verbatim_quote: For minor plumbing work not requiring cutting into or removal of piping, a permit is not required. You may contact the Department of Building Inspection, Inspection Services - Plumbing Inspection Division at (628) 652-3450 for more information regarding permit requirements.
facts.verification: OFFICIAL-VERIFIED (verbatim) — but taken from the City of San Francisco's archived October 2020 edition of the DBI FAQ because the live sfdbi.org URL redirects to sf.gov and could not be read — see FL-02

facts.statement: Under the California Building Standards Code no building or structure may be erected, constructed, enlarged, altered, repaired, moved, improved, removed, converted or demolished unless a separate permit has first been obtained from the building official, and the requirement is administered locally.
facts.verbatim_quote: According to the California Building Standards Code, no building or structure may be erected, constructed, enlarged, altered, repaired, moved, improved, removed, converted or demolished unless a separate permit for each building or structure has first been obtained from the building official. Code requirements vary in different cities and counties around the state. Check with your local building department to find out what's needed in your area.

facts.topic: Who may pull a permit in San Francisco
facts.statement: DBI's online permit system requires a valid California contractor licence; plumbing contractors must hold a C-4 or C-36 licence to obtain a plumbing permit, general building contractors must hold a B licence to schedule building permit inspections or apply for a kitchen/bath remodel permit, and DBI confirms the company name matches the contractor licence number and business licence number.
facts.verbatim_quote: All users must have the following: 1. Valid California Contractor License... Plumbing contractors must have: C4 or C36 license to obtain plumbing permit. General Building contractors must have: B License to schedule Building permit inspections or apply for Kitchen/Bath remodel permit.
facts.verification: OFFICIAL page; text captured from the official page's indexed content rather than a direct render — see FL-03

facts.statement: Under the DBI plumbing/mechanical fee schedule in force for permits issued on or after 12 July 2026: Category 1P (single residential unit — single plumbing fixture installation or a single kitchen or bathroom remodel, maximum two inspections) is; regular inspections are /hour, off-hour inspections /hour, and a re-inspection per half hour.
facts.verbatim_quote: CATEGORY 1P | Single Residential Unit – water service, sewer replacement, single plumbing fixture installation, shower pan installation, or a single kitchen or bathroom remodel (maximum two inspections) |... Hourly issuance/inspection rates of per hour for regular inspections and per hour for off-hour inspections... Re-inspection or additional inspection per Section 108A.8, shall be per half hour.

facts.statement: DBI requires a separate permit for each structure, condominium unit, existing apartment unit, high-rise office floor, suite or tenant space.
facts.verbatim_quote: A separate permit is required for each structure, condominium unit, existing apartment unit, high-rise office floor, suite, or tenant space.

facts.statement: C-36 Plumbing covers the supply of water and the disposal of fluid waste and, in its terms, the maintenance and replacement of those items and the associated safety devices.
facts.verbatim_quote: A plumbing contractor provides a means for a supply of safe water, ample in volume and of suitable temperature for the purpose intended and the proper disposal of fluid waste from the premises in all structures and fixed works.... (f) The maintenance and replacement of all items described above and all health and safety devices... (832.36 CCR)

facts.statement: C-9 is the drywall classification; a drywall contractor installs gypsum wall board and assemblies including nonstructural metal framing and performs the taping and texturing to produce a continuous smooth or textured surface.
facts.verbatim_quote: A drywall contractor lays out and installs gypsum wall board and gypsum wall board assemblies including nonstructural metal framing members, and performs the taping and texturing operations including the application of compounds that adhere to wall board to produce a continuous smooth or textured surface.

facts.topic: When a general contractor must subcontract a trade
facts.statement: A residential remodeling contractor (B-2) may contract for drywall and for plumbing fixtures, but may not install, replace, substantially alter or extend plumbing systems unless it holds the appropriate licence classification or subcontracts to an appropriately licensed subcontractor.
facts.verbatim_quote: A residential remodeling contractor shall not contract to install, replace, substantially alter, or extend electrical, mechanical, or plumbing systems or their component parts, or the mechanisms or devices that are part of those systems, unless the residential remodeling contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts to an appropriately licensed subcontractor. (BPC §7058 / 832.61 CCR)

facts.topic: Landlord entry into an occupied unit
facts.statement: A landlord may enter to make necessary or agreed repairs, must give reasonable written notice stating the date, approximate time and purpose, may enter only during normal business hours unless the tenant consents, and 24 hours is presumed reasonable notice (6 days if the notice is mailed). No notice is required in an emergency or where the tenant is present and consents.
facts.verbatim_quote: (a)(2) To make necessary or agreed repairs... (d)(1)... The notice shall include the date, approximate time, and purpose of the entry.... Twenty-four hours shall be presumed to be reasonable notice in absence of evidence to the contrary.... Mailing of the notice at least six days prior to an intended entry is presumed reasonable notice... (e)(1) To respond to an emergency. (e)(2) If the tenant is present and consents to the entry at the time of entry.

facts.topic: Home improvement contract and payment rules
facts.statement: CSLB's published consumer guidance for home improvement projects requires a fixed-price contract and limits down payments to no more than or 10% of the contract price, whichever is less.
facts.verbatim_quote: Contractors must use a fixed price contract. A fixed-price contract lists the full agreed upon price for the project.... Down payments should be no more than or 10%.... These rules apply to all home improvement projects.
facts.verification: OFFICIAL-VERIFIED (text as published on the CSLB home page and press release)

facts.topic: What a licence record proves and what it does not
facts.statement: Each CSLB licence-detail page shows business information, licence status, classifications, contractor's bond and workers compensation, and states the date the data was last refreshed; complaint disclosure is restricted by law and only appears on the page when it exists.
facts.verbatim_quote: Data current as of 11/6/2026 5:24:49 AM... CSLB complaint disclosure is restricted by law (B&P 7124.6)... Due to workload, there may be relevant information that has not yet been entered into the board's license database.

facts.topic: Landlord maintenance duty for rented units
facts.statement: The 2025 San Francisco Housing Code is the code that governs maintenance of rented dwelling units in San Francisco and is administered by DBI.

facts.topic: How to reach the permitting and inspection authority
facts.statement: DBI Customer Service is (628) 652-3200; permit fee estimates are handled by the Central Permit Bureau at dbi.cpbrequest@sfgov.org or (628) 652-3240; permit applications and status are handled through the PermitSF portal.
facts.verbatim_quote: DBI Customer Service 628-652-3200... Permit Processing Support dbi.cpbrequest@sfgov.org... Track the permit you obtained through the PermitSF portal
